subject: Post-demo: Next-stage model slate + decision kit
messages:
From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@novus.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 15:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + follow-ups

Thanks for the walkthrough today — helpful to see the latency profiles and the canary behavior. A few things we agreed to surface:
- A compact shortlist of recommended models tuned for our 1) realtime chat UI (95th pct SLO: 250ms) and 2) async batch scoring job (throughput priority).
- Benchmarks for our 2 payload types (short queries ~40 tokens, long context ~600 tokens).
- A starter prompt set we can use for regression checks post-rollout.

I'm looping procurement (procurement@novus.ai) to get an estimate for committed vs burst pricing; they may ask for the SKU breakdown. Can you send the shortlist + quick cost/latency tradeoff table?

Appreciate it,
Alex
Product Lead, Novus AI

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Alex Cho <alex.cho@novus.ai>, procurement@novus.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + follow-ups

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Posting the shortlist below (we focused on models that strike different points on cost/latency/quality so you can pick the operational knob that matters most):

Recommended shortlist (summary):
1) regio-7B-quant (low-latency, cost-efficient) — good for short-query UIs. 95th pct tail latency at 40 tokens: ~95ms on dedicated p4dn; quality: very good for extraction/completion but weaker on long-form coherence.
2) cedar-13B-pt (balanced) — mid cost, strong quality across long contexts. 95th pct at 600 tokens: ~420ms; better instruction-following and fewer hallucinations on QA prompts.
3) atlas-30B-int8 (high-quality, higher cost) — best long-context performance and factuality in our evals; 95th pct at 600 tokens: ~670ms; recommended for mixed-critical flows where precision outweighs cost.

Attached I’m including: novus_demo_benchmarks.csv (raw runs), cost-latency-matrix.pdf (summary table), and a starter prompt pack prompt-set-novus-v1.txt. We also added a very small regression harness: 30 prompts that catch hallucination/regression risk for your domain.

Tradeoff notes (short):
- If your priority is sub-250ms 95th for chat, regio-7B-quant with prefix caching + aggressive batching is the pragmatic starting point, then route longer jobs to cedar or atlas.
- If you want a single-model solution to reduce routing operational complexity, cedar-13B-pt is the sweet spot. It’s ~1.8x cost of regio but reduces fallback surface.
- Atlas-30B-int8 buys the best quality for edge-case legal/finance language at ~3.5x cost vs regio.

Next actions proposed:
- Internal: Ben to confirm memory/quantization notes and provide expected per-token cost delta (Ben: can you confirm the cost assumptions I used in the sheet?).
- Customer: Alex to confirm which flow (chat first vs batch-first) they want Redwood to prioritize for a pilot.
- Procurement: we’ll prepare a 90-day committed SKU quote and a burst-only alternative.

Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: novus_demo_benchmarks.csv (csv), cost-latency-matrix.pdf (pdf), prompt-set-novus-v1.txt (text)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Alex Cho <alex.cho@novus.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + follow-ups

Quick technical clarifications and calibration from the infra side:
- regio-7B-quant: benchmarked with int4 quant on A100-80GB and trimmed KV to 2.1M entries; expect slightly higher tail on p4dn (we saw ~120ms at 95th in p4 runs). We should call out that for 40-token bursts the batching savings make it cheapest in practice.
- cedar-13B-pt: uses a fused attention kernel that helps long-context throughput; we recommend a "slim" KV cache config to keep memory headroom when you concurrently run batch scoring.
- atlas-30B-int8: runs best with 2x model sharding on multi-GPU nodes; the cost in the sheet assumes dedicated pools. If you want a private deployment, we can tighten the cost delta.

Prompt/regression notes: the starter prompt set includes 30 high-sensitivity cases (hallucination anchors, adversarial paraphrases, and legalese snippets). We recommend you run the 30-case regression after any model/quant change and then a 200-case smoke suite weekly.

Ben Carter
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none; see dielectric notes in novus_demo_benchmarks.csv]

From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@novus.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novus.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + follow-ups

Thanks — that’s exactly what we needed. Quick answers:
- Pilot path: Chat-first, prioritized (we want to validate UX latency). If chat-first shows too many regressions on long-form workflows, we’ll expand to the hybrid routing approach.
- Procurement: please send a 90-day committed quote for regio-7B-quant + cedar-13B-pt as the fallback; include per-token and per-hour reserved vs burst SKU lines.
- Req: Can you add a short paragraph to the sheet listing the rollback guardrails (model switch latency, cache warm-up expected time, traffic split plan)? That will help our SRE team sign off.

Next steps for Redwood: send the committed SKU quote + an operational runbook (1 pager) describing rollout, rollback, and regression gating.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the quote.
Alex
Product Lead, Novus AI
